turn.context: The first Automations turn: how the build works. From bed-management.md §7.4.1 (the engine, a to e, and the 2 PM and 6 PM passes), §7.2 (the records) and §7.4.2 (discharge first, read access), with the transcript’s own facts.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · “How would the build work?” (the record stops at 31)

sample.name: The build, step by step
sample.what: The station panel from the Automations landing page. Two main switches on top, one row of four lamps for each automation. Step through the four steps of the build and the lamps light in order.

text: Here is the build, in the order it happens.
bullets: First, read access. Your IT team links the systems that already hold admissions, discharges, inpatient notes and billing. We write nothing back.
Second, discharge. The bed plan runs on discharge times, so discharge is built and linked before the bed mapping.
Then one engine does five jobs. It maps tomorrow’s beds and ICU beds, checks discharge times, holds emergency beds back and sets call-in times.
chat.invite: Pick any part to see what it reads and what it makes. Or tell me which systems your hospital runs.
chat.note: Read access and discharge first. The engine comes after.
prompts: What exactly would our IT team do?
Why must discharge be built first?
What if some records are on paper?
chat.pointer: Step through the build. The lamps light as each automation moves from idea to switched on. Pick a row to open it.

sheets.text: Each of the five admission steps is stamped as it happens. That shows paperwork apart from waiting.

sheets.text: One report joins bill close and bill open against the same bed. Your own number, before anything else changes.

sheets.text: Tested while the two jobs start running together. Switched on once the discharge times it uses are real.

sheets.title: Discharge times checked
sheets.text: Discharge is built first in step 4. The engine checks its times against the beds as they free.

lines.label: Why first

sheets.title: Tomorrow’s bed map
sheets.text: Built on top of discharge. A first pass at 2 PM and a final freeze at 6 PM, every day.

lines.label: Makes
lines.value: One bed for each planned admission

sheets.entry: How many planned admissions on a usual day?

hand.does: Checks the 6 PM freeze before it goes out.

sheets.title: ICU bed map
sheets.text: The same mapping for ICU beds, using step-down signals given by 1 PM.
sheets.entry: How many ICU beds do you run?

sheets.title: Emergency beds held back
sheets.text: A number of beds is kept for emergencies, worked out from two to three years of your own admissions.

lines.label: Makes
